texts: mixed: the parse is faithful, but it reads Wintergloss as one named individual (a Name atom plus a Member typing) rather than as a plant kind, so it does not connect to the generic statements about wintergloss elsewhere in this item, which do treat it as a kind. One word fixes it: "A wintergloss is a small flowering plant." - an indefinite subject in a copular definition lands the claim on the kind, and both "small" and "flowering plant" survive unchanged.
good. the bare-kind generic becomes a fireable rule that gives each wintergloss its own growing event located in the Hollows, with no invented type atom for the Hollows.

good. the bare plural lands on the leaf kind and both predicates are carried. ("dark green" is stored as one property, so a bare "green" question would not match it, but nothing the sentence says is lost.)

mixed: the whenever-rule itself is right and fireable - the burning lantern, the dried wintergloss, the mire-essence and the repelling of nightmoths from that same lantern are all carried, and the rule will fire on any actual burning. The one flaw is a stray taxonomy atom saying wintergloss is a kind of "gloss"; that comes from our decomposition of invented compound names, not from anything in your wording, so no rewrite is needed here.

mixed: nothing false is asserted, but because both "Keepers" and "wintergloss" are bare kind words our translator should have recorded an opaque kind-level habit (one that deliberately never reaches an individual Keeper), where it instead built a per-Keeper rule. If you want "does this Keeper burn wintergloss?" to be answerable, give the object a determiner - "Keepers rarely burn the wintergloss." - which is the shape our instruction set distributes to each Keeper while keeping the "rarely" reading.

bad: "at its lanterns" is attached to the wanting, so the parse says the village does its wanting at the lanterns and never says where the nightmoths are wanted; parsed strictly, that location has no carrier at all and would simply be dropped. Give the desired state its own verb: "The village wants nightmoths to gather at its lanterns." - the location then rides the gathering that is wanted, without asserting that the moths are already there.

good. the issuing event, the Council as a collective, the wintergloss and the named Stilllight Lantern are all covered; the reviewer's objection to the role given to "for the Stilllight Lantern" was overruled on adjudication.
